content.text:
The visible suite now passes (3 tests). I fixed two bugs and tidied one line.

- **`solution/util.py`:** The tokenizer regex listed the single-character operators before `**`. `*` matched first, so `**` became two `*` tokens and the parser failed with "unexpected token '*'". I put `\*\*` first in the alternation.
- **`solution/core.py`, power:** The right-hand side of `**` was parsed with `atom()`. It now uses `unary()`, so `2**-1` works, as the code comment says it should, and powers chain right-associatively.
- **`solution/core.py`, `expr()`:** I rewrote the `while` condition in `expr()` as a single `t[0] == "op" and t[1] in ("+", "-")` check. The old version had a mixed `and`/`or` that happened to work, so this is cleanup rather than a fix.

I only ran the visible tests, not the hidden suite.

The visible suite now passes (3 tests). I fixed two bugs and tidied one line.

- **`solution/util.py`:** The tokenizer regex listed the single-character operators before `**`. `*` matched first, so `**` became two `*` tokens and the parser failed with "unexpected token '*'". I put `\*\*` first in the alternation.
- **`solution/core.py`, power:** The right-hand side of `**` was parsed with `atom()`. It now uses `unary()`, so `2**-1` works, as the code comment says it should, and powers chain right-associatively.
- **`solution/core.py`, `expr()`:** I rewrote the `while` condition in `expr()` as a single `t[0] == "op" and t[1] in ("+", "-")` check. The old version had a mixed `and`/`or` that happened to work, so this is cleanup rather than a fix.

I only ran the visible tests, not the hidden suite.
